workload.problem: damped harmonic oscillator x'' + 2 zeta omega x' + omega^2 x = 0, classical RK4, fixed step (perf_card.py)

arm_labels.eagle_term8: eagle host, termination loop, up to 8 threads
arm_labels.eagle_compact8: eagle host, termination + compaction, up to 8 threads
arm_labels.eagle_reorder8: eagle host, termination + compaction + reorder, up to 8 threads
arm_labels.eagle_reorder1: eagle host, termination + compaction + reorder, 1 thread

arms.eagle_term8: The GPU card's eagle graph arm, unchanged, on the host: the same hawk step kernel, eagle.deploy and eagle.until_done call, run by eagle's OpenMP host team; one code base for GPUs and CPUs. On this card: spread S=100, N=1,000,000: 14.4 ms; spread S=1000, N=1,000,000: 142 ms; uniform S=1000, N=1,000,000: 187 ms. Fastest in 12 of 12 cells.
arms.eagle_term1: The same loop on one thread: the difference to the 8-thread row is the threading alone. On this card: spread S=100, N=1,000,000: 114 ms (7.91× eagle 8-thread time); spread S=1000, N=1,000,000: 1.13 s (7.95× eagle 8-thread time); uniform S=1000, N=1,000,000: 1.49 s (7.97× eagle 8-thread time). Fastest in 0 of 12 cells.
arms.eagle_compact8: The GPU card's compaction arm on the host: the launch covers only the samples still running, the map rebuilt every 16 steps when a sample finished. On this card: spread S=100, N=1,000,000: 38.4 ms (2.68× eagle 8-thread time); spread S=1000, N=1,000,000: 292 ms (2.06× eagle 8-thread time); uniform S=1000, N=1,000,000: 744 ms (3.97× eagle 8-thread time). Fastest in 0 of 12 cells.
arms.eagle_compact1: The compaction loop on one thread: the difference to the 8-thread row is the threading alone. On this card: spread S=100, N=1,000,000: 164 ms (11.4× eagle 8-thread time); spread S=1000, N=1,000,000: 1.03 s (7.28× eagle 8-thread time); uniform S=1000, N=1,000,000: 3.56 s (19× eagle 8-thread time). Fastest in 0 of 12 cells.
arms.eagle_reorder8: The GPU card's reorder arm on the host: the live samples moved to the front of every plane when they spread thin, restored to sample order at the end (inside the wall). On this card: spread S=100, N=1,000,000: 74.6 ms (5.2× eagle 8-thread time); spread S=1000, N=1,000,000: 242 ms (1.71× eagle 8-thread time); uniform S=1000, N=1,000,000: 761 ms (4.07× eagle 8-thread time). Fastest in 0 of 12 cells.
arms.eagle_reorder1: The reorder loop on one thread: the difference to the 8-thread row is the threading alone. On this card: spread S=100, N=1,000,000: 196 ms (13.6× eagle 8-thread time); spread S=1000, N=1,000,000: 877 ms (6.18× eagle 8-thread time); uniform S=1000, N=1,000,000: 3.58 s (19.1× eagle 8-thread time). Fastest in 0 of 12 cells.
arms.numba_prange: Compiles a plain Python loop to machine code with no separate language; each sample keeps its state in registers across all of its steps and stops on its own, so finished samples cost nothing. On this card: spread S=100, N=1,000,000: 32.4 ms (2.26× eagle 8-thread time); spread S=1000, N=1,000,000: 328 ms (2.31× eagle 8-thread time); uniform S=1000, N=1,000,000: 1.53 s (8.16× eagle 8-thread time). Fastest in 0 of 12 cells.
arms.jax_shard8: The JAX arm spread over 8 CPU devices: the batch is sharded and each shard runs its own vmapped while loop, with no cross-shard step synchronisation. On this card: spread S=100, N=1,000,000: 194 ms (13.5× eagle 8-thread time); spread S=1000, N=1,000,000: 1.86 s (13.1× eagle 8-thread time); uniform S=1000, N=1,000,000: 1.94 s (10.4× eagle 8-thread time). Fastest in 0 of 12 cells.
arms.jax_vmap: Compiles the whole loop once and batches a per-sample while loop with vmap; the same code runs on GPUs and differentiates with jax.grad. On this card: spread S=100, N=1,000,000: 296 ms (20.6× eagle 8-thread time); spread S=1000, N=1,000,000: 2.74 s (19.3× eagle 8-thread time); uniform S=1000, N=1,000,000: 2.88 s (15.4× eagle 8-thread time). Fastest in 0 of 12 cells.
arms.torch_masked: Runs the masked array version on a multi-threaded tensor library; it fits where the computation already lives next to a PyTorch model or needs autograd. On this card: spread S=100, N=1,000,000: 1.06 s (73.7× eagle 8-thread time); spread S=1000, N=1,000,000: 10.2 s (72.2× eagle 8-thread time); uniform S=1000, N=1,000,000: 10.2 s (54.5× eagle 8-thread time). Fastest in 0 of 12 cells.
arms.numpy_masked: No compile step and no dependency beyond NumPy; masked array code computes every sample every step, so it fits dense batches where all samples run to the end (the uniform configuration). On this card: spread S=100, N=1,000,000: 1.64 s (114× eagle 8-thread time); spread S=1000, N=1,000,000: 15.3 s (107× eagle 8-thread time); uniform S=1000, N=1,000,000: 13.4 s (71.4× eagle 8-thread time). Fastest in 0 of 12 cells.
arms.mp_numpy: Spreads NumPy over processes with the standard library alone; each chunk stops once its own samples are done. On this card: spread S=100, N=1,000,000: 782 ms (54.5× eagle 8-thread time); spread S=1000, N=1,000,000: 7.72 s (54.4× eagle 8-thread time); uniform S=1000, N=1,000,000: 7.65 s (40.9× eagle 8-thread time). Fastest in 0 of 12 cells.
arms.python_loops: Nothing to install and each line can be stepped in a debugger; run only at small N here. On this card: spread S=100, N=10,000: 38.7 ms (243× eagle 8-thread time); spread S=1000, N=10,000: 362 ms (241× eagle 8-thread time); uniform S=1000, N=1,000: 166 ms (792× eagle 8-thread time). Fastest in 0 of 12 cells.
